content:
Noah: Quick sync — Prospect Nimbus wants proof they can swap VendorX for Redwood with minimal client changes. They want: a small compatibility shim, token billing reconciliation vs VendorX's 50-token bucketing, and a filled security questionnaire (CMK preference). Can we scope a lean POC?
Rina: I can run the parity checks. Ask: can they share a week of logs (anonymized) and the six canonical prompts? We should show tokenization deltas and output diffs.
Tom: I'll own the shim. Plan: accept VendorX-style payloads (body field `input_text`) and headers `X-VendorX-Session` + `X-VendorX-Client`. Translate to Redwood API with conversation_id, populate KV from session store, then call model. Will provide a compatibility mode that emits `choices[].text` and `usage.total_tokens`.
Helena: Security side: they require SOC2, audit logs, IP allowlist, retention controls and prefer customer-managed KMS. Hosted can support CMK with extra paperwork and a dedicated workspace. I'll draft the answers. Also they asked if we can redact PII fields before log ingestion.
Noah: Nimbus expects a demo Thursday. Can we have runnable artifacts by Wed EOD (prototype adapter repo + short diff report + security answers + cost delta)?
Rina: Parity notes: VendorX uses a different tokenizer (variant BPE) so token counts may differ; sampling defaults also differ. We'll test with deterministic sampling (top_k=1, seed fixed) and a non-deterministic run to show live variance.
Tom: Example adapter mapping (pseudo):
```
POST /compat/vendorx/generate
Headers: {"Authorization":"Bearer <t>", "X-VendorX-Session":"s-42", "X-VendorX-Client":"mobile-ios"}
Body: {"input_text":"<user prompt>", "max_tokens":120}
```
Adapter: map `input_text` -> `prompt`, fetch session s-42 -> KV={last_3_msgs}, call Redwood: /v1/generate {prompt, conversation_id: s-42} -> transform response -> {choices:[{text}], usage:{prompt_tokens:.., completion_tokens:.., total_tokens:..}}
Tom: Compatibility toggle: `?compat=vendorx_v1` to enable legacy fields like `choices[].logprobs` (nullable) and `finish_reason`. Keep `logprobs` off by default.
Helena: On logprobs: returning token-level logprobs is considered sensitive by some customers. We can support it behind contract for Dedicated/Private. For hosted, we require approvals and include perf impact notes.
Noah: Billing translation: VendorX bills per-request rounding up to 50-token buckets. Redwood bills per token. We need a script to convert their historical bills into Redwood estimates and produce a simple delta chart (p95, median).
Rina: I'll run tokenization on their sample prompts and their logs (if they provide) and produce a small table of per-prompt token deltas and a projected monthly cost difference. Expect variance ~ -5% to +12% depending on prompt profile.
Tom: Latency caveat: shim adds ~10ms for header lookup + KV assembly if sessions cached; on miss could add ~40-60ms. We'll show both numbers.
Helena: KMS: we support CMK for Dedicated and Private. Hosted CMK requires a dedicated workspace and security approval. I'll outline steps and an estimated calendar for approvals (~2-4 weeks).
infra-bot: Note: enabling customer-managed KMS on hosted triggers a security review and network isolation checklist. See internal runbook link (internal only).
Noah: Edge-case: VendorX sometimes returns `choices[0].metadata` with model/debug fields clients rely on. We recommend the shim synthesize a `metadata` object with minimal fields (model_name, model_version, token_estimate) to avoid client breakages.
Rina: Action items: 1) Tom -> prototype shim repo + demo curl (Tue PM). 2) Rina -> parity diffs for 6 prompts (Wed AM). 3) Helena -> security Q doc + CMK path + PII redaction note (Tue noon). 4) Noah -> assemble demo deck + billing sim slide.
Tom: Example curl for demo:
```
curl -X POST https://demo.redwood/compat/vendorx \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer demo-token" \
  -H "X-VendorX-Session: s-42" \
  -d '{"input_text":"Create a 2-sentence summary of last quarter","max_tokens":60}'
```
Response will mimic VendorX shape and include `usage.total_tokens` for their billing UI.
Rina: Parity caveat: tokenizer alignment can be mitigated by pre-tokenizing inputs with VendorX tokenizer in the shim and passing the raw token ids to Redwood when allowed, but that has portability implications. We'll note it as an optional compatibility hack.
Helena: For PII redaction: we can enable pre-ingest redaction rules (regex + named-entity heuristics) for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can request redaction rules but need to accept potential recall issues.
Noah: OK team — drop links to artifacts here as they land. Nimbus wants low friction; emphasize minimal client changes and a clear fall-back (canary routing to VendorX for a % of traffic during cutover). Ping me when items are uploaded. :rocket:
